item.title: MALVEAUX: From Reconstruction to the SAVE Act — The Politics of Paperwork
item.description: Frederick Douglass claimed his identity in a system that denied him documentation, and today's debates over the SAVE Act ask whether we will let the state decide who counts in democracy. item.title: BOOK REVIEW: ‘I’ll Make Me a World: The 100-Year Journey of Black History Month’ by Jarvis R. Givens
item.description: "I'll Make Me a World" by Jarvis R. Givens tells the story of how Black History Month was established in 1926 by Carter G. Woodson and how it has evolved over the years, while also providing a timeline of Black history from the 19th century to the present day. The post BOOK REVIEW: ‘I’ll Make Me a World: The 100-Year Journey of Black History Month’ by Jarvis R. Givens appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.description: Marlon Calhoun, senior point guard for the KIPP DC Legacy Prep Bulldogs, is leading his team into playoffs while balancing his obligations on the court and in the classroom, and is inspiring his teammates with his leadership and humility. item.title: Ramadan is Underway: Here’s What Local Mosques Have Planned

item.title: With Arrival in D.C., Monks Promote Power of Peace After 2,300-Mile Walk
item.description: Buddhist monks completed a 2,300-mile Walk for Peace from Fort Worth, Texas to Washington, D.C. to promote mindfulness, kindness, reflection and unity, inspiring many to choose harmony over winning and to practice mindfulness in their daily lives. item.title: Maryland Ends Local ICE Partnerships as Governor Signs Emergency Immigration Law
item.description: Maryland Gov. Wes Moore has signed emergency legislation barring state and local law enforcement agencies from entering into agreements with federal immigration authorities that allow officers to carry out civil immigration enforcement duties, effectively ending the state's participation in the 287(g) program. The post Maryland Ends Local ICE Partnerships as Governor Signs Emergency Immigration Law appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Most Surgery Patients Don’t Finish Critical At-Home Therapy: Study
item.description: A new survey from The Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center found that 76% of surgical patients did not complete their prescribed at-home physical therapy exercises, which can delay healing and jeopardize surgical outcomes. The post Most Surgery Patients Don’t Finish Critical At-Home Therapy: Study appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Ben Crump’s Courtroom Doc Earns Emmy Honor
item.description: Ben Crump, along with filmmakers Cameron S. Mitchell and Raji Ramanathan and director John Beder, won a regional Emmy for producing the short documentary "How to Sue the Klan", which tells the story of five Black women in Chattanooga who used the 1871 Ku Klux Klan Act to successfully sue the Ku Klux Klan in 1982. The post Ben Crump’s Courtroom Doc Earns Emmy Honor appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Maryland’s Van Hollen Leads Democrats Planning State of the Union Boycott
item.description: Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D) of Maryland will not attend President Donald Trump's upcoming State of the Union address, instead joining fellow Democrats at a protest rally on the National Mall near the U.S. Capitol to protest the president's policies. The post Maryland’s Van Hollen Leads Democrats Planning State of the Union Boycott appeared first on The Washington Informer.
